req.title: Login required for create
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /create.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-012 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who attempt GET /create are redirected to /auth/login with a 302 status. The violation was that test[0] was labelled kind=negative but heuristic=EP. A negative test must use heuristic=NEG. Fix: change test[0] heuristic from EP to NEG, which is correct because the test exercises the error pathway (anonymous access denied) rather than a valid equivalence partition. Tests 1 and 2 are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_anonymous_get_create_redirects_to_login
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temporary database
No session cookie is present (anonymous client)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/create')
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
    f"Expected redirect to /auth/login, got {r.headers.get('Location')}"
)

tests.name: test_authenticated_get_create_returns_200
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temporary database seeded with user Rahul/stone
Client is logged in as Rahul
actions: Send GET /create with the authenticated session
expected: GET /create returns exactly 200 (no redirect to login)
trace: R-FLASKR-012: authenticated user → GET /create → 200 (guard does NOT redirect)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}
)
assert login_r.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {login_r.status_code}'
r = client.get('/create')
assert r.status_code == 200, (
    f'Expected 200 for authenticated user, got {r.status_code}'
)

tests.name: test_logout_then_get_create_redirects_again
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temporary database seeded with user Rahul/stone
Client logs in, then logs out, returning to anonymous state
expected: Location header after logout attempt is exactly /auth/login
trace: R-FLASKR-012: state transition anonymous→authenticated→anonymous; boundary is the session boundary
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()
login_r = client.post(
    '/auth/login',
    data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}
)
assert login_r.status_code == 302
r_auth = client.get('/create')
assert r_auth.status_code == 200, (
    f'Expected 200 while authenticated, got {r_auth.status_code}'
)
logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert logout_r.status_code == 302
r_anon = client.get('/create')
assert r_anon.status_code == 302, (
    f'Expected 302 after logout, got {r_anon.status_code}'
)
assert r_anon.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
    f"Expected /auth/login, got {r_anon.headers.get('Location')}"
)
